name: sain

attributes.attribute: the concept of making a place holy to remove pagan associations
the saint who sained many Irish holy wells with his staff

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Sain is an Irish and Scottish concept. The word means roughly to make holy. It names the acts of saints who took pagan associations from a sacred place. Saint Patrick of Ireland dipped his pastoral staff in many holy wells. His act let ritual continue at the sites under Christian protection. Once a place was sained, people held it safe against evil spirits and fairies. Those beings were seen as old forms of Celtic and pre-Celtic divinities. Saining joined the old holy places to the new faith.

okr.objective: Document sain, the act of making a place holy.
key_results: Record the meaning of sain as to make holy.
Record Saint Patrick's saining of holy wells.
